newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: December start for FMC 's Argentine lithium.
newsitem.headline: December start for FMC 's Argentine lithium.

text.p: The Fenix lithium mine being developed by U.S. firm FMC Corp in northern Argentina will start its first mine production in December, the mine's general manager said Monday.

"We're going to start putting brine through the first part of the plant, which is the first ore out of the mine, probably some time in December," Gonzalo Tufino, of local subsidiary FMC Minera del Altiplano, told Reuters by telephone.
He said the first output of lithium compounds will probably come in the first few months of 1997, after a process of solar evaporation.
"We are already testing and commissioning the brine production system," he said. "The system will be commissioned and checked in the coming week."
To be the first of a wave of modern Argentine mines to enter into production, the $68 million Fenix project will produce 45 million pounds, lithium carbonate equivalent, a year.

The mine is being built on the Salar del Hombre Muerto salt lake straddling the border of the provinces of Catamarca and Salta. FMC said earlier in 1996 that the startup of Fenix will allow it to close its plant in Bessamer City, North Carolina, some time next year.
Located at 13,000 feet (4,000 meters) above sea level, Fenix will provide the first major lithium production outside Chile or the United States.

The mine's output will enter a long cozy lithium market now frazzled by the aggressive marketing of Chilean newcomer Sociedad Quimica y Minera de Chile (Soquimich). Soquimich announced in February that it will sell lithium at around 30 percent below the going world rate.

The largest consumers of lithium carbonate, a fine white powder, are the glass, ceramics and primary aluminum industries. Demand is also strong from U.S. smelters where lithium is used for improving energy efficiency. It is used, in smaller quantities, as a treatment for manic depression.
